summary: Go ReadMcpResourceTool matches the canonical name, visible server/uri parameters, concurrency-safe marker, deferred discovery metadata, and the basic live JSON-RPC resources/read call. It is not yet fully parity-aligned with the TS reference. The main gaps are output normalization and robustness rather than the happy-path request itself: Go returns a stringified legacy MCP envelope instead of the TS declared output shape, can inline or truncate binary blobs instead of writing blobSavedTo entries, has a direct HTTP GET fallback that bypasses MCP resources/read semantics, lacks TS connected-state and capabilities gating, does not clear/reconnect stale resource-read clients the way TS ensureConnectedClient/onclose does, and does not expose the TS read-only, max-result, output-schema, and auto-classifier metadata for this tool.

gaps.title: Go returns a legacy raw MCP envelope rather than the exact TS output schema
gaps.description: TS declares and returns exactly {contents:[{uri,mimeType?,text?,blobSavedTo?}]}. Its mapper constructs a new contents array and intentionally emits only uri, optional mimeType, text, and blobSavedTo-derived fields. Go currently returns ToolResult.Content as the JSON string from renderMCPResourceResult(raw), which preserves the server's resources/read envelope with legacy transformations. This means Go can expose extra fields such as blob, type, annotations, or _meta, can preserve top-level _meta that TS drops, and has no typed outputSchema equivalent for callers to rely on.

ts_evidence.note: The output schema is an object with contents[], where each item contains uri, optional mimeType, optional text, and optional blobSavedTo only.
The call path maps each returned content item into the TS output shape and ignores fields outside that shape.
The model-facing tool_result content is jsonStringify(content), i.e. the normalized TS output object.

go_evidence.note: Execute calls resources/read via CallRaw and returns ToolResult{Content: renderMCPResourceResult(raw)}.
renderMCPResourceResult preserves the raw top-level envelope, including _meta when present, and renders each item through the legacy raw item renderer.
Go ToolResult is a string/content-block container and does not carry a typed ReadMcpResource output object or output schema.
Current tests assert a JSON envelope with contents but do not assert the exact TS field whitelist.

gaps.impact: Callers and the model can see a different JSON contract from TS, especially for non-trivial MCP resource items. Exact consumers would need Go-specific parsing.

gaps.title: Binary resource blobs are not converted to TS-style blobSavedTo entries on the tool execution path
gaps.description: TS decodes every resources/read blob, writes the raw bytes to the tool-results directory with a MIME-derived extension, and returns blobSavedTo plus a short text notice. Go has binary persistence helpers and a rich resource renderer, but ReadMcpResourceTool does not use that rich renderer. Its current legacy renderer can leave small binary blobs inline as base64 or truncate large base64 into a JSON item with binary_truncated/original_size_bytes, neither of which matches TS and both of which can pollute model context.

ts_evidence.note: Blob contents are decoded from base64, persisted with persistBinaryContent, and returned as blobSavedTo plus getBinaryBlobSavedMessage text.
persistBinaryContent writes raw bytes to the tool-results directory with a MIME-derived extension.
getBinaryBlobSavedMessage produces the short saved-path text returned in the resource output.

go_evidence.note: ReadMcpResourceTool uses renderMCPResourceResult, not renderMCPResourceToolResult or persistMCPBlobToBlocks.
The legacy resource renderer returns JSON strings rather than TS blobSavedTo objects.
renderMCPContentItem only truncates large binary data and otherwise returns raw items, so small blob fields can remain inline.
A richer resource renderer exists and can produce content blocks and persistence behavior, but it is not wired into ReadMcpResourceTool.Execute.
Binary persistence tests cover renderMCPCallToolResult, not ReadMcpResourceTool.Execute.

gaps.impact: Binary MCP resources can leak base64 into the model context, lose the TS blobSavedTo field, and become hard to consume with downstream file-aware tools.

gaps.title: HTTP fallback reads /resources/<uri> directly instead of using MCP resources/read semantics
gaps.description: TS always performs an MCP resources/read request through a connected MCP client, including HTTP servers via the SDK StreamableHTTP transport. Go's AddServer compatibility path bypasses JSON-RPC and performs a direct GET against /resources/<uri>, then returns the raw response body. This changes method, URL encoding, auth/session behavior, response shape, output limits, and binary handling.

ts_evidence.note: The tool reads resources by issuing method resources/read with params {uri} through the connected MCP client.
TS HTTP MCP servers are connected through StreamableHTTPClientTransport with auth provider and request headers, not through REST /resources paths.
The result is returned through the same normalized output object regardless of transport.

go_evidence.note: When conn.client is nil and httpBaseURL is set, ReadMcpResourceTool delegates to mcpHTTPGet.
mcpHTTPGet constructs GET baseURL/resources/<resourceURI>, reads at most 1 MiB, and returns the raw body.
AddServer installs this HTTP-mode connection without a JSON-RPC MCP client.

gaps.impact: Simple HTTP-mode servers produce non-TS output, cannot return MCP contents[] envelopes consistently, and can behave differently from real streamable HTTP MCP servers.

gaps.title: Go lacks TS-equivalent connected-state and resources capability gating
gaps.description: TS receives a runtime list of MCP clients with explicit connected/failed/needs-auth/pending/disabled states. ReadMcpResourceTool first finds a runtime client by name, rejects non-connected clients, and rejects connected clients that do not advertise capabilities.resources before sending resources/read. Resource helper tools are also added to the visible tool set only when at least one connected server supports resources. Go always registers ReadMcpResourceTool at setup and its Execute path attempts Connect(server), then calls resources/read regardless of advertised capabilities because MCPServerConn does not store capabilities.

ts_evidence.note: MCPServerConnection is a union of connected, failed, needs-auth, pending, and disabled states; connected clients carry capabilities.
The tool errors if the named server is absent, not connected, or lacks capabilities.resources.
Resource helper tools are appended only when a connected client supports resources.
The connection-attempt path likewise gates ListMcpResourcesTool and ReadMcpResourceTool on supportsResources.

go_evidence.note: Go registers ReadMcpResourceTool unconditionally whenever the MCP manager is created.
MCPServerConn stores config, client, tools, ready, and httpBaseURL, but no server capabilities or connection-state union.
Connect starts or reuses a server, lists tools, and stores a ready connection without persisting initialize capabilities.
ReadMcpResourceTool Execute connects and calls resources/read without checking resources capability.
The newer services client can expose capabilities, but tools/mcp_tools.go is not using that surface.

gaps.impact: The tool can be visible or executable in sessions where TS would hide or reject it earlier, and unsupported resources fail later with server-specific JSON-RPC errors instead of the TS message.

gaps.title: Resource reads do not get TS-style stale-session/onclose cache clearing and reconnect semantics
gaps.description: TS installs onerror/onclose handlers that close failed transports, reject pending calls, clear connection and fetch caches, and make ensureConnectedClient reconnect on subsequent tool/resource calls. Go's MCPManager returns any ready cached connection; the stdio restart helper is not wired into Connect, and there is no equivalent onclose/session-expired path that deletes a stale connection before retrying resources/read. A failed resources/read can therefore keep using the same cached connection until explicit Shutdown or manual deletion.

ts_evidence.note: TS wraps close handling so transport close rejects pending tool calls and leads to cache clearing.
HTTP session expiry is detected and triggers transport close/reconnection.
onclose clears connection, tool, resource, command, and skill caches.
ensureConnectedClient obtains a fresh connected client after cache clearing.

go_evidence.note: Connect immediately returns a cached connection when conn.ready is true.
resources/read errors are surfaced as ToolResult errors; the cached connection is not cleared or retried.
A WatchStdioForRestart helper exists, but it requires an external done channel.
The restart loop deletes the server and calls Connect, but only if the watcher is actually started.
Repository search shows WatchStdioForRestart is defined but not called from Connect or setup.

gaps.impact: A server restart, closed stream, or expired HTTP session can leave ReadMcpResourceTool stuck on a stale connection instead of recovering like TS.

gaps.title: Go does not expose ReadMcpResourceTool's read-only, classifier, output-schema, and result-budget metadata
gaps.description: TS marks ReadMcpResourceTool as read-only and concurrency-safe, defers it for tool search, provides a searchHint, caps model-facing results at 100000 characters, exposes an outputSchema, converts the input to `${server} ${uri}` for auto classification, and reports truncation based on the JSON output. Go has the name, schema, concurrency-safe marker, and registry-level shouldDefer/searchHint fallback, but the general Tool interface and this tool do not expose read-only status, max result size, output schema, user-facing name, result-truncation predicate, or auto-classifier input.

ts_evidence.note: TS declares concurrency safety, read-only status, auto-classifier input, shouldDefer, searchHint, and maxResultSizeChars=100000.
TS exposes inputSchema and outputSchema from the tool definition.
TS wires render/user-facing/result-truncation/result-block mapping hooks.
ReadMcpResourceTool is in the TS auto-mode safe allowlist.

go_evidence.note: Go exposes Name, Aliases, IsConcurrentSafe, Description, and input Schema only.
The Go Tool interface requires only Name, Description, Schema, and Execute.
Registry metadata marks ReadMcpResourceTool deferred with a search hint, but does not include read-only, result-budget, classifier, or output-schema metadata.
The repository architecture notes identify missing isReadOnly, max result-size, shouldDefer, and related Tool metadata in Go.
The Go permission checker evaluates tool names and inputs, but it has no per-tool read-only/classifier metadata path for ReadMcpResourceTool.

gaps.impact: The Go runtime cannot make the same permission, discovery, truncation, and typed-output decisions for this tool that TS can make.

gaps.title: Runtime input acceptance and validation messages are broader than the TS contract
gaps.description: The model-visible Go schema has server and uri, which matches TS at the surface. Runtime parsing is broader: Go also accepts server_name/resource_uri aliases, trims whitespace, and has explicit empty-field errors. TS accepts only server and uri in the tool schema, does not trim before lookup, and empty strings flow into the same not-found/not-connected checks as any other string. This is a smaller schema/runtime drift, but it matters for exact replay and error parity.

ts_evidence.note: The TS input schema only defines server and uri as strings.
The TS call path uses server and uri directly and reports a server-not-found error when the server name has no match.
The prompt documents only server and uri.

go_evidence.note: ReadMcpResourceInput includes legacy server_name/resource_uri alongside server/uri.
Execute trims server/uri, falls back to aliases, and emits server is required / uri is required for blank values.
Current tests assert Go-specific missing-server and missing-uri error text.
Current parsing tests cover the legacy server_name/resource_uri alias shape.

gaps.impact: Most model calls still work, but TS/Go exact replay and error snapshot tests will diverge on aliases and blank/whitespace inputs.

gaps.title: Current tests do not lock the high-risk ReadMcpResourceTool parity edges
gaps.description: Go has useful happy-path resources/read tests and renderer-level tests, but the tool execution path is not covered for TS-exact field whitelisting, binary blobSavedTo output, no base64 leakage, HTTP fallback normalization, capabilities gating, stale connection recovery, or read-only/result-budget metadata. Existing parity tests even assert the current raw contents envelope rather than the TS-normalized output constraints.

ts_evidence.note: The TS output schema provides the field-level contract that should be tested.
TS capability gating and resources/read request behavior are explicit enough to lock with tests.
TS binary persistence behavior is explicit and currently not covered at the Go tool execution layer.
TS metadata behavior should be covered by Go metadata tests once metadata exists.

go_evidence.note: ReadMcpResourceTool tests cover text success, URI passing, and multi-content, but not binary, exact field whitelist, capabilities, HTTP fallback, or lifecycle recovery.
Binary persistence tests exercise renderer helpers rather than ReadMcpResourceTool.Execute.
The enforced parity contract currently checks uri/mimeType/text in a contents envelope but not the full TS ReadMcpResourceTool output semantics.
The binary_resource_persistence contract is still marked pending-red-skip.

gaps.impact: Future changes can appear to pass the current suite while still violating the highest-risk TS behaviors for resource reads.

candidate_tasks.title: Normalize ReadMcpResourceTool output to the TS contents schema
candidate_tasks.description: Replace the legacy raw-envelope return for resources/read with a TS-shaped normalizer that emits only {contents:[{uri,mimeType?,text?,blobSavedTo?}]}. Preserve existing text and multi-content behavior, but drop raw blob, _meta, annotations, type, and other MCP fields from this tool's model-facing JSON unless a later TS source starts exposing them.
acceptance: ReadMcpResourceTool.Execute returns valid JSON with top-level contents and TS-whitelisted item fields only.
Text resources preserve uri, optional mimeType, and text exactly.
Empty raw results continue to return {"contents":[]}.
Top-level _meta, per-item annotations/_meta/type, and raw blob/data fields do not appear in the ReadMcpResourceTool output unless converted by a TS-compatible rule.
Existing successful text and multi-content tests continue to pass.

candidate_tasks.title: Persist binary resources and return TS-style blobSavedTo entries
candidate_tasks.description: Teach the ReadMcpResourceTool execution normalizer to decode resources/read blob content, persist raw bytes with the existing MIME-derived extension helper, and return blobSavedTo plus the saved-content text notice. Ensure base64 never appears in model-facing resource-read output.
acceptance: Binary resource blobs are decoded from base64 and written as raw bytes under the configured MCP tool-results directory.
The JSON output item includes uri, optional mimeType, blobSavedTo, and text matching the saved-content message shape.
The original base64 blob/data is absent from ToolResult.Content for small and large binaries.
Persist failures return a text field saying binary content could not be saved, matching the TS behavior class.
MIME-derived extensions match existing TS/Go MIME extension mappings.

candidate_tasks.title: Align HTTP-mode resource reads with MCP resources/read output semantics
candidate_tasks.description: Remove or quarantine the direct GET /resources/<uri> fallback for ReadMcpResourceTool. For HTTP-backed MCP servers, use a JSON-RPC resources/read path when possible; if AddServer compatibility must remain, normalize its response into the same TS-shaped contents output and preserve the structured OAuth-required hint for 401s.
acceptance: HTTP-backed ReadMcpResourceTool calls no longer return arbitrary raw HTTP response bodies for successful reads.
Successful HTTP-mode resource reads return the same TS-shaped contents object as stdio/live MCP reads.
HTTP 401 still returns the existing structured oauth_required error envelope with WWW-Authenticate preserved.
URI values containing slashes, schemes, and query strings are not reinterpreted as unsafe REST path segments.
Existing MCPTool HTTP OAuth tests continue to pass.

candidate_tasks.title: Gate ReadMcpResourceTool on connected server state and resources capability
candidate_tasks.description: Store MCP initialize capabilities and connection state in the Go MCP manager/tool layer, then make ReadMcpResourceTool match TS: absent server, non-connected server, and connected-without-resources produce distinct early errors, and resource helper exposure is gated on at least one server advertising resources.
acceptance: MCPServerConn or an equivalent services-layer record stores server capabilities from initialize.
ReadMcpResourceTool refuses connected servers without resources capability before issuing resources/read.
ReadMcpResourceTool preserves a TS-like distinction among server not found, server not connected, and resources unsupported.
The model-visible helper tool is not added in contexts where no connected MCP server supports resources, matching TS resourceTools gating.
Existing MCP resource-read happy path remains unchanged for resources-capable servers.

candidate_tasks.title: Clear stale MCP connections and retry resource reads after session close or expiry
candidate_tasks.description: Wire Go's MCP connection lifecycle so closed stdio/SSE/HTTP sessions are removed from MCPManager caches and the next ReadMcpResourceTool call reconnects like TS ensureConnectedClient. Detect session-expired errors where possible, reject or surface current failed calls, and avoid returning a permanently stale ready connection.
acceptance: Connect does not return a cached ready connection after the underlying client has closed or reported a terminal session error.
A resources/read error classified as session expired clears the cached connection so a subsequent call reconnects.
The stdio restart watcher is actually attached for subprocess-backed MCP clients or replaced with an equivalent integrated lifecycle path.
Reconnect success refreshes the tool/resource-capability state used by ReadMcpResourceTool.
No goroutine leaks or repeated stale-client reuse in close/reconnect tests.

candidate_tasks.title: Expose ReadMcpResourceTool read-only, classifier, output-schema, and result-budget metadata
candidate_tasks.description: Add a local Go metadata surface for ReadMcpResourceTool that can represent the TS contracts: read-only=true, shouldDefer=true, searchHint, maxResultSizeChars=100000, output schema, user-facing name readMcpResource, result-truncation predicate, and auto-classifier input `${server} ${uri}`. Hook the metadata into registry/tool search and permission/risk paths where those concepts already exist.
acceptance: ReadMcpResourceTool can be queried as read-only by the Go permission/risk layer.
ToolSearch/discovery metadata includes the TS-aligned search hint and deferral semantics.
A max result size of 100000 characters is available to the result handling layer or explicitly enforced for this tool.
An output schema equivalent to the TS contents schema is available in Go metadata.
Auto-classifier input for server=fs uri=memo://a is exactly "fs memo://a" after TS-equivalent input normalization.

candidate_tasks.title: Decide and lock exact TS input validation semantics for ReadMcpResourceTool
candidate_tasks.description: For exact replay parity, align runtime validation with the TS server/uri-only schema or explicitly quarantine legacy aliases behind compatibility tests. This is lower priority because the model-visible schema already uses server/uri, but it should be made intentional rather than accidental.
acceptance: The visible input schema documents only server and uri.
Whitespace, blank strings, unknown fields, and legacy aliases have explicit tests documenting whether Go intentionally matches TS or preserves compatibility.
If exact mode is chosen, server_name/resource_uri no longer alter ReadMcpResourceTool behavior in normal execution.
If compatibility aliases remain, they are documented as Go compatibility behavior and do not leak into the model-facing schema or classifier input.

candidate_tasks.title: Add focused TS parity tests for ReadMcpResourceTool edge behavior
candidate_tasks.description: Create red/green tests that lock the TS ReadMcpResourceTool contract independently of broad MCP alignment tests. Cover TS output field whitelist, blobSavedTo persistence, no base64 leakage, HTTP-mode normalization, resources capability gating, stale-connection recovery, metadata, and input validation decisions.
acceptance: Tests fail on the current implementation for each high-risk gap that remains unfixed.
Tests include TS evidence comments pointing to ReadMcpResourceTool.ts and relevant MCP client/storage code.
Tests use local in-process MCP servers or httptest servers only; no network credentials or external MCP services are required.
The suite can be run independently with a narrow go test command before and after implementation tasks.
